public_inputs.detail: Finite dimension, tracked explicitly and never hidden in a constant; known exactly
Maximum order of a complete jet. Fix $k\ge2$ before varying the remaining parameters; its value is known.
Global Lipschitz upper bound for the kth derivative; a known admissible upper bound
Known upper bound on the initial distance to some global minimizer; in the ball-constrained specification, the known ball radius
Known objective-gap tolerance
Higher-order Lipschitz complexity exponent $2/(3k+1)$, computed from public parameters
Known initial point.

auxiliary_interfaces: The geometry and membership test of the known ball are free. Known regularized Taylor and mirror models may be minimized globally within the ball at no charge.

source_fields.unit_cost: Each complete jet costs one unit, under a fixed worst-case call budget. Tensor operations, linear algebra, and global solution of known regularized models are free; this is not an arithmetic-time complexity measure.
free_operations: Internal operations and global solution of known models
Exact real arithmetic, unlimited memory, and arbitrarily small positive query separations; limit values are not treated as oracle responses

view_override_policy.limitations: Mechanical merge does not certify consistency or mathematical identity. Narrative qualifications and source conditions remain authoritative.

source_fields.uniformity: One algorithm must work for all admissible instances and oracle laws; an average guarantee over a hard distribution alone is insufficient.

description_paragraphs: The base error is
$$\mathcal{E}(\widehat{x})=f(\widehat{x})-f^*.$$
Here $f^*=\inf_{x\in Q}f(x)$. The lower-boundedness or attainment assumption makes this error finite and nonnegative.
Return $\widehat{x}\in Q$.
The output may be an unqueried point, a feasible average of past iterates, or another feasible postprocessing result. No function value or additional computable certificate is required.
The objective $f$ is convex and $C^k$ on an open convex neighborhood of the closed ball $Q=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:\|x-x_0\|_2\le R\}$, with $k\ge2$. The optimization domain is $Q$.
Regularity holds for every pair of points in this neighborhood. A minimum exists on the closed ball; no additional promise places an unconstrained minimizer inside the ball.

description_paragraphs: Each primitive response specified under ORACLE costs one unit. Queries at new points introduced by any inner procedure also count toward the total.
The resource budget is a fixed worst-case cap on every execution path. Initialization, stopping checks, and all actual responses in a batch are included.
Arithmetic, linear algebra, tensor operations, storage, and global solution of known models are free. Bit complexity, communication, and wall-clock time are not counted.

description_paragraphs: Each query selects $x$ in $Q$ and returns the complete exact tuple $J_{k}f(x)=(f(x),Df(x),\ldots,D^{k}f(x))$. The fixed objective uniquely determines the response, with no stochastic noise.
A description of the feasible set, feasibility tests and global minimization of known models formed from existing replies are supplied as public auxiliary operations.

The public inputs are $x_0$, the target accuracy, and $d$, $k$, $M_k$, $R$, $\varepsilon_f$. Numerical constants are admissible bounds and need not equal the sharp constants of the instance. The objective, unqueried derivatives, minimizer and minimum value are hidden.
Solve $\min_{x\in Q}f(x)$ to obtain an objective-value approximation relative to the global infimum.
